title: TokenPhase-aware kernel allocator and routing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a kernel allocator and routing layer that reasons about token phase (prefill vs decode), per-request token-phase distribution, and architecture fingerprints to pick kernels with the best joint latency/cost tradeoff. The allocator will combine phase-sliced microprofiles with a lightweight online tuner to avoid regressing tail latency during decode while preserving batching efficiency during prefill.
background: Current kernel selection is predominantly per-model and coarse-bucketed by sequence length. We observe mismatches for workloads with skewed token-phase profiles (short prefill, long decode or vice versa). These mismatches cause suboptimal kernel choices: either slower decode tail latency (when chosen for prefill throughput) or wasted GPU cycles (when chosen for decode safety). Server-side experiments and customer incidents (notably a chat product regression last quarter) motivate a more phase-aware allocation strategy.
proposal:
1) Collect phase-sliced microbenchmarks for each candidate kernel on each architecture we support (A100, H100 family variants, T4/GPU class) capturing: prefill throughput, decode p50/p95/p99, memory footprint, and kv-cache behavior.
2) Build a tokenizer-phase profile per request (estimated prefill tokens vs expected decode tokens) using prompt metadata + lightweight sampling.
3) Use a two-stage allocator:
   - Fast filter: eliminate kernels that violate hard constraints (OOM, incompatible ops, lack of required attention optimization).
   - Bandit tuner: a constrained bandit that optimizes expected cost with a latency fairness constraint (maintain decode p95 within configured margin for the customer tier). The bandit uses phase-sliced reward signals.
4) Safety: if tuner uncertainty is high, fall back to a conservative kernel set (high-confidence low-regret kernels) for that tenant until warmstart evidence is collected.
5) Control plane APIs to pin kernel preference per model/tenant and to surface the allocator decision rationale in the Console.
success_metrics:
- Reduce decode p95 tail regressions for mixed-phase chat workloads by >= 20% relative to baseline kernel selector.
- Reduce average per-token GPU cost across mixed workloads by >= 8% for uncovered models.
- Maintain prefill throughput within 5% of baseline for billing-sensitive customers.
- <1% of requests should trigger conservative fallback in steady-state for top-tier customers.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable allocator for internal workloads in staging, collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (internal beta): enable for 10% of internal production traffic; run bandit in exploration mode only (no live switches) for 1 week.
- Phase 3 (customer beta): enable routing decisions for 5 pilot customers (opt-in) with conservative fallback and dashboard transparency.
- Phase 4 (gradual roll): increase exposure using automated rollback if decode p95 exceeds configured thresholds.
Rollout will include an escape hatch to pin to previous kernel selection per model via the Console.
implementation_notes:
- Extend microbenchmark harness (ENG-27105) to emit phase-sliced results and KV cache warm/cold profiles.
- Add telemetry fields: decision_reason, tuner_confidence, estimated_phase_ratio, selected_kernel_id.
- Tuner should be implemented as a pluggable service with a REST/GRPC API; initial implementation will be in Go to match runtime runtime services.
- Use Thompson-sampling-like constrained bandit with safety envelope; keep exploration budget per model small (configurable).
- Persist per-model kernel preference and exploration history in tenant metadata store with TTL to avoid noisy cold starts.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator filtering logic and fallback.
- Integration tests: replay recorded request traces with simulated architectures to verify decision stability.
- Performance QA: microbench harness runs across all supported kernels and arch profiles.
- Chaos tests: forcibly induce high-latency kernel to ensure fallback and rollback work.
- Add telemetry-driven alerts for increased decode p95 or sudden cost regressions.
risks:
- Incorrect phase estimation for dynamically generated prompts could lead to poor kernel choices.
- Bandit exploration risks causing tail spikes in decode latency for customers in early rollout.
- Microbenchmarking overhead and storage of phase-sliced profiles may increase infra cost.
- Complexity of decision surface across many arches may require pruning of kernel candidates.
mitigations:
- Conservative fallback and exploration limits per tenant.
- Feature flag with per-tenant control and immediate pinning via Console.
- Start with a small set of vetted kernels (3 per arch) and expand.
- Profile-based retention policy for microbench data; use sampling for long-tail models.
acceptance_criteria:
- Allocator selects kernel and records decision_reason for >99% of requests in canary.
- Bandit service runs in exploration mode without making live kernel switches in internal beta.
- In customer beta, decode p95 does not exceed baseline + configured margin for pilot customers; engineering-run dashboards show meaningful confidence signals.
- Documentation describing control plane flags, Console UX, and rollback steps published in Confluence (link below).
open_questions: What is the minimal metadata footprint required to estimate phase ratio at request arrival?
Should we include a model-level hint API to allow SDKs to provide expected decode length?
What is a safe exploration budget per model for top-tier customers?
How to prioritize kernels when memory and latency tradeoffs conflict across arches?
